questions.prompt: A 49 year old client, Mr. David Miller, is admitted to the medical-surgical unit with dehydration. The healthcare provider orders an intravenous fluid bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride at 150 mL/hour for 4 hours. The nurse prepares to administer the infusion.

structure.stem: A 49 year old client, Mr. David Miller, is admitted to the medical-surgical unit with dehydration. The healthcare provider orders an intravenous fluid bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride at 150 mL/hour for 4 hours. The nurse prepares to administer the infusion.
structure.prompt: A 49 year old client, Mr. David Miller, is admitted to the medical-surgical unit with dehydration. The healthcare provider orders an intravenous fluid bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride at 150 mL/hour for 4 hours. The nurse prepares to administer the infusion.
calculation_steps: Identify the ordered infusion rate (150 mL/hour) and the duration of the infusion (4 hours).
Multiply the infusion rate by the duration to find the total volume.

rationale.trap: A common trap is incorrectly dividing the rate by the duration or adding them, rather than multiplying, leading to an incorrect total volume calculation.
rationale.golden_rule: Always double-check dosage calculations, especially for IV fluids, to prevent medication errors and ensure patient safety.
rationale.core_concept: Accurate medication and fluid administration requires precise dosage calculations to ensure patient safety and therapeutic effect.
rationale.answer_analysis: To determine the total volume, the nurse multiplies the infusion rate (mL/hour) by the total duration of the infusion (hours), yielding 150 mL/hour * 4 hours = 600 mL.
